corrected_answer:
For scenario variant 5, treat the intermittent OOM as an unproven symptom and preserve a safe baseline before changing capacity controls. Reproduce the immutable request trace with cold and warm caches while changing one factor at a time: prompt tokens, generated tokens, concurrency, batching, request lifetime, cancellation, timeout, retry, and prefix reuse. First distinguish true device exhaustion from reserved-but-unusable memory, fragmentation, KV retention/leak, host-pinned spill, or faulty accounting.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at fixed configuration, peak allocated and reserved device memory is approximately bounded by a prespecified per-live-KV-token slope plus fixed overhead, and returns within a prespecified tolerance after requests complete. Collect synchronized request lifecycle events, input/output/KV token counts, KV bytes by layer/cache pool, active sequences and batch composition, allocator allocation/free/reservation events, evictions, prefix-cache hits, retries, cancellations, OOM exception context, GPU/CPU/host-pinned memory, utilization, power, and temperature.

Run a randomized, paired one-factor experiment with at least five independent repetitions per prespecified stratum, excluding warm-up only by a declared rule. Fit memory versus live KV tokens and report peak allocated, reserved, fragmentation ratio, OOM rate, post-drain residual, latency, throughput, and correctness with denominators and uncertainty intervals. Keep correctness checks independent; do not treat a successful response as proof of no leak. Confounders include allocator warm-up and bins, CUDA graph/workspace caches, asynchronous frees, clock drift, background GPU use, thermal throttling, variable generation lengths, retries, and cache eviction.

Canary changes behind a feature flag, alert on OOM rate, residual memory, fragmentation, P99 latency, correctness, and queue growth, and auto-rollback to the pinned safe configuration on any predeclared threshold breach. Evidence required before attributing cause: synchronized allocator/KV traces, a reproduced failure, and a post-drain memory test across cancellation and retry paths. Pin and record model revision, precision, context and max-batch limits, GPU count/type, driver/runtime, allocator, KV layout, scheduler, prefix-cache policy, admission, and software build; report measured bytes and tokens separately, and label estimates. Reproduce the immutable request trace with cold and warm caches while changing one factor at a time: prompt tokens, generated tokens, concurrency, batching, request lifetime, cancellation, timeout, retry, and prefix reuse. First distinguish true device exhaustion from reserved-but-unusable memory, fragmentation, KV retention/leak, host-pinned spill, or faulty accounting.

Falsifiable hypothesis: at fixed configuration, peak allocated and reserved device memory is approximately bounded by a prespecified per-live-KV-token slope plus fixed overhead, and returns within a prespecified tolerance after requests complete. Falsify it if residual memory keeps increasing after live KV tokens return to baseline, the slope changes unexpectedly by workload stratum, or an allocation fails despite adequate aggregate free memory because of fragmentation. Collect synchronized request lifecycle events, input/output/KV token counts, KV bytes by layer/cache pool, active sequences and batch composition, allocator allocation/free/reservation events, evictions, prefix-cache hits, retries, cancellations, OOM exception context, GPU/CPU/host-pinned memory, utilization, power, and temperature.

Run a randomized, paired one-factor experiment with at least five independent repetitions per prespecified stratum, excluding warm-up only by a declared rule. Fit memory versus live KV tokens and report peak allocated, reserved, fragmentation ratio, OOM rate, post-drain residual, latency, throughput, and correctness with denominators and uncertainty intervals. Keep correctness checks independent; do not treat a successful response as proof of no leak. Confounders include allocator warm-up and bins, CUDA graph/workspace caches, asynchronous frees, clock drift, background GPU use, thermal throttling, variable generation lengths, retries, and cache eviction.

Mitigate in priority order: cap context/max output and concurrency; enforce token-and-memory admission with headroom and per-tenant quotas; bound batch/live sequences and reject or queue safely; then test paged KV, bounded prefix caching/eviction, allocator tuning, and KV quantization only with an independent quality/correctness comparison. Canary changes behind a feature flag, alert on OOM rate, residual memory, fragmentation, P99 latency, correctness, and queue growth, and auto-rollback to the pinned safe configuration on any predeclared threshold breach. Evidence required before attributing cause: synchronized allocator/KV traces, a reproduced failure, and a post-drain memory test across cancellation and retry paths. Unknown platform details and thresholds must be measured or explicitly marked evidence_required.
risks: OOM may have multiple interacting causes; a single-factor replay can miss allocator or scheduler interactions
mitigations such as quantization or cache changes can alter correctness, latency, or isolation
platform-specific thresholds are unknown until measured
evidence_required: synchronized allocator and KV-cache traces
reproducible failure with post-drain memory accounting
independent correctness and paired performance results across cancellation, timeout, retry, and cache states
